mainTopic: Betrothing with מעשר שני and הקדש: רבי יוחנן's two reasons, and רב חסדא's rule that a mistaken use of הקדש takes no effect
overview: This amud first finishes a discussion about מעשר. The גמרא asks why a separate verse is needed, and רבין סבא answers that the word "הוא" teaches that the item stays in its holy state. Next comes the משנה's argument about betrothing with הקדש. רבי מאיר says it works if done on purpose, and רבי יהודה says it works if done by mistake. רבי יעקב reports two reasons from רבי יוחנן for the cases where the woman is not betrothed. In one case only she objects, and in the other they both object. רבי ירמיה and רבי יעקב each match these reasons to מעשר and הקדש in opposite ways. Then רב חסדא rules that, for רבי מאיר, a mistaken use of הקדש money does nothing: the money stays holy, and even a purchase does not take effect. A challenge from a משנה about a storekeeper is answered: there רבי מאיר was only arguing on רבי יהודה's terms. The amud ends as רב begins to explain the reasons behind the משנה's dispute, and his words continue on the next amud.

steps.title: Why do we need a separate source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the previous derivation. It argues that the point should already be understood on its own from the verse just discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't you already understand this on your own from that verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the earlier learning. It says we should already know this point without a new source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse just discussed compares the Jewish people to תרומה and calls it "holy". So the label "holy" seems to follow automatically, and the גמרא asks what an extra source adds. The question is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge.

phrases.english: But don't you understand it by itself from it?
phrases.notes: "It" is the verse just discussed, the one comparing the Jewish people to תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous section about the holiness of מעשר and תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a separate derivation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the verse already calls it holy, the point is automatic, so an extra source seems unneeded.

steps.title: The word "הוא" teaches that it stays as it is
steps.stepSummary: רבין סבא explains before רב that the extra point comes from the word "הוא" ("it is"). It means the item stays in its holy state.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין סבא explained it before רב: The verse says "It is", which means it must stay as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין סבא answers the challenge by pointing to one word in the verse about מעשר. That word teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "הוא" teaches that the מעשר remains in its holy status as it is. So the source is not extra after all, because it adds this specific detail.

keyTerms.meaning: it shall be as it is

phrases.english: Ravin the Elder explained it before Rav:
The verse says: "It is"
As it is, it shall be.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies an extra word in the verse that teaches a new detail.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source seemed unneeded because holiness was already clear.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word "הוא" teaches that the item stays in its holy state, so it adds something new.

steps.title: The משנה on betrothing with הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. רבי מאיר says betrothal with הקדש works if done on purpose but not by mistake. רבי יהודה says the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with consecrated property: if he did it on purpose, she is betrothed. If he did it by mistake, she is not betrothed. This is the view of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: if by mistake, she is betrothed. If on purpose, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה about a man who betroths a woman with Temple property (הקדש).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא gives the opposite ruling for the same two cases, on purpose (מזיד) and by mistake (שוגג). The reasons are not given here. This line sets up רבי יעקב's report about the cases where the woman is not betrothed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. In this case רבי מאיר says it works on purpose, while רבי יהודה says it works by mistake.

phrases.english: And with consecrated property: intentionally, he has betrothed;

phrases.aramaic: בְּשׁוֹגֵג – לֹא קִידֵּשׁ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: unwittingly, he has not betrothed. These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says: unwittingly, he has betrothed;
intentionally, he has not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: הקדש on purpose works, by mistake does not. רבי יהודה: by mistake works, on purpose does not.

steps.title: רבי יעקב reports two rulings from רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב says he heard two rulings from רבי יוחנן. In the mistaken מעשר case of רבי יהודה and the mistaken הקדש case of רבי מאיר, the woman is not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said: I heard two things from רבי יוחנן. The mistaken-מעשר case of רבי יהודה and the mistaken-הקדש case of רבי מאיר: in both, the woman is not betrothed with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב points to two specific cases where the woman is not betrothed. He is preparing to give רבי יוחנן's reasons for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases are mistakes (שוגג): one is רבי יהודה's view on מעשר שני, and the other is רבי מאיר's view on הקדש. רבי יעקב groups them together because רבי יוחנן explained both.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב: שְׁמַעִית מִינֵּהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן תַּרְתֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov said: I heard two things from Rabbi Yochanan:
an unwitting case of tithe according to Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: In the earlier משנה, רבי יהודה said that betrothing with מעשר שני by mistake does not work.

phrases.english: and an unwitting case of consecrated property according to Rabbi Meir –
in both of them, a woman is not betrothed with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב: שְׁמַעִית מִינֵּהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks out cases from the משנה for explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the mistaken-מעשר case (רבי יהודה) and the mistaken-הקדש case (רבי מאיר), there is no betrothal.

steps.title: Two reasons, but which goes with which?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gave two reasons. In one case, the woman does not want it. In the other, neither of them wants it. רבי יעקב does not remember which reason belongs to which case.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is because the woman does not want it, and the other is because neither of them wants it. And I don't know which is which.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב gives the two reasons but admits he forgot how to match them to the cases. This sets up an open question for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that betrothal fails when the people involved would not want it done this way. One reason depends only on the woman's unwillingness, and the other depends on both sides. The next two steps try to work out which case gets which reason.

phrases.english: One – because the woman does not want it,
and one – because neither of them wants it,
and I don't know which of them is which.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons for the cases in step 4 and raises the matching problem.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reason (woman alone, or both) applies to מעשר, and which applies to הקדש?

steps.title: רבי ירמיה matches the reasons by logic
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה reasons it out. With מעשר, only the woman objects, because of the trip to ירושלים, while the man is happy to acquire a wife at no cost. With הקדש, both object to causing Temple property to lose its holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Let us look at it ourselves. With מעשר, she is not happy because of the bother of the trip, but he is happy that he acquires a wife at no cost. But with הקדש, neither of them wants Temple property to lose its holiness through them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers רבי יעקב's question with logic. He gives "woman alone" to מעשר and "both" to הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני must be eaten in ירושלים, so she must carry it there, but he pays nothing of his own. With הקדש, using it makes it lose its holiness, and neither person wants to be responsible for that.

keyTerms.meaning: let us look at it ourselves
it pleases her, she is happy with it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: Let us see for ourselves:
With tithe – she is not pleased with it
because of the trouble of the journey,
phrases.notes: מעשר שני can only be eaten in ירושלים, so she would have to bring it there.

phrases.aramaic: אִיהוּ נִיחָא לֵיהּ דְּנִיקְנֵי אִיתְּתָא מִמֵּילָא.
phrases.english: but he is pleased that he acquires a wife by itself.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הֶקְדֵּשׁ – תַּרְוַיְיהוּ לָא נִיחָא לְהוּ
phrases.english: But with consecrated property – neither of them is pleased
that consecrated property should lose its holiness through them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the matching question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With מעשר, only the woman objects. With הקדש, both object.

steps.title: רבי יעקב argues the opposite makes more sense
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב argues the reverse. With מעשר, he also objects, because of the risk of loss on the road. With הקדש, he would be happy to acquire a wife at no cost, so only she objects.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יעקב said: The opposite makes more sense. Can't we say that with מעשר, she is unhappy because of the bother of the trip, and he is unhappy because of mishaps on the road? But with הקדש, it is true that she doesn't want Temple property to lose its holiness through her, but wouldn't he be happy to acquire a wife at no cost?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב rejects רבי ירמיה's matching and shows that the reverse match is just as logical, or even more so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He flips both cases. With מעשר, the man also worries the produce may be lost on the way, which would leave her with nothing. With הקדש, the man gets a wife without spending, so he has no objection. This shows that logic alone cannot settle the matching.

keyTerms.meaning: a mishap or accident on the road

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's two reasons (only the woman objects, or both object) cannot be clearly assigned to מעשר and הקדש by logic. רבי ירמיה and רבי יעקב each make a reasonable case for opposite matches.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yaakov said: The opposite is more reasonable.
Isn't it possible to say:
with tithe, she is not pleased
because of the trouble of the journey,

phrases.aramaic: אִיהוּ לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם אוּנְסָא דְאוֹרְחָא?!
phrases.english: and he is not pleased because of a mishap on the way?!
phrases.notes: If the מעשר gets lost on the way, she ends up with nothing, and he doesn't want that.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הֶקְדֵּשׁ, בִּשְׁלָמָא אִיהִי לָא נִיחָא לַהּ
phrases.english: But with consecrated property, granted she is not pleased
that consecrated property should lose its holiness through her,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִיהוּ מִי לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ
phrases.english: but wouldn't he be pleased
to acquire a wife by itself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי ירמיה's matching from step 6 and offers the reverse.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי ירמיה's assignment of reasons to the two cases.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The man also has a reason to object with מעשר (risk of loss), and has no reason to object with הקדש (a free acquisition).

steps.title: Does the money lose its holiness if the betrothal fails?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב חסדא: according to רבי מאיר the woman is not betrothed with הקדש money given by mistake, but does the money itself become חולין?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב חסדא: The woman is not betrothed. But what about the money? Does it go out to חולין?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a follow-up question about רבי מאיר's ruling. We know the woman is not betrothed, so what happens to the הקדש money that was handed over?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when someone uses הקדש for his own benefit by mistake, the הקדש loses its holiness and becomes חולין. רבא wants to know whether that still happens here, even though the betrothal itself failed.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a formal question to a teacher)
Lose their holiness and become ordinary (non-sacred)

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Chisda:
The woman is not betrothed;
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר's ruling from step 3: הקדש used by mistake does not betroth.

phrases.english: what about the money: does it go out to non-sacred status?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יוחנן discussion and asks a new question about רבי מאיר's ruling from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הקדש money becomes חולין even though the betrothal did not take effect.

steps.title: No betrothal, so the money stays holy
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers: since the woman is not betrothed, the money cannot lose its holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The woman is not betrothed. So how could the money go out to חולין?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the money stays הקדש. If the betrothal did nothing, the money did nothing either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money only loses its holiness if it was actually put to use. Here the betrothal failed, so the money accomplished nothing, and nothing changed about its status.

keyTerms.meaning: Misuse of Temple property, which makes it lose its holiness

phrases.english: He said to him:
The woman is not betrothed,
so how could the money go out to non-sacred status?

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The money does not become חולין, because the betrothal never took effect and so the money was never really used.

steps.title: What about buying something with הקדש money?
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין asks רב חסדא whether the same rule applies to a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין asked רב חסדא: What is the law with a sale?
steps.whatsHappening: A second student asks whether a purchase made by mistake with הקדש money also fails to take effect, just as the betrothal fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Betrothal might be special, since a woman may not want to be betrothed in such a way. The question is whether an ordinary purchase made by mistake with הקדש money also does not work according to רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Avin asked Rav Chisda:
What is the law with a sale?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the question from betrothal to a sale.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a purchase made by mistake with הקדש money takes effect according to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: A sale does not work either
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that even with a sale, the buyer does not acquire the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even with a sale, he does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא says a sale works the same way as betrothal. The purchase does not take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This widens רבי מאיר's rule. A mistaken use of הקדש money does not take effect at all, whether for betrothal or for buying something. This is the claim the גמרא will now challenge.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Even with a sale, he does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַף בְּמֶכֶר לֹא קָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sale question from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A sale made by mistake with הקדש money does not take effect either.

steps.title: A challenge from the case of the storekeeper
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין brings a משנה where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue whether a storekeeper is treated like a homeowner or like a money changer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: A storekeeper is like a homeowner. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: A storekeeper is like a money changer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין starts a challenge by quoting a משנה from מסכת מעילה. This step only quotes the source. The next step will show why it is a problem for רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is about someone who leaves money with another person, and the money turns out to be הקדש. A שולחני is allowed to spend loose deposited money, but a בעל הבית may not. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about which of these a חנווני is like.

phrases.english: He challenged him:
A storekeeper is like a homeowner,
phrases.notes: This is the end of a longer teaching about money left with someone. A homeowner may not spend it, but a money changer may spend loose coins.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
A storekeeper is like a money changer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an objection to רב חסדא's answer in step 11 by quoting a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that, according to רבי מאיר, a sale made by mistake with הקדש money does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the source is quoted here, and the inference against רב חסדא comes in the next step.

steps.title: Everyone agrees that spending the money is מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue only about how to treat a storekeeper. Both agree that if the money was spent, מעילה happened, so the purchase must have worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only argue about this: one master holds a storekeeper is like a money changer, and the other holds a storekeeper is like a homeowner. But everyone agrees: if he spent it, he committed מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: This step pins down the challenge. The משנה shows that even רבי מאיר agrees that spending the הקדש money counts as מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה only happens if the spending actually worked and the money really left הקדש. So if רבי מאיר agrees there is מעילה when the money is spent, then a purchase made by mistake with הקדש money must take effect. That goes against רב חסדא, who said even a sale does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argue up to this point (about nothing more)

phrases.english: They only argue
about this: one master holds a storekeeper is like a money changer,
and the other master holds a storekeeper is like a homeowner.
But according to everyone:
if he spent it, he committed misuse of Temple property!
phrases.notes: Misuse only counts if the spending worked, so the purchase must have taken effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the problem out of the משנה quoted in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling in step 11 that a mistaken sale with הקדש money does not take effect according to רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even רבי מאיר agrees that spending the money is מעילה. מעילה requires a purchase that worked, so a mistaken sale with הקדש money does take effect.

steps.title: רבי מאיר was only arguing on רבי יהודה's terms
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר does not truly agree that spending is מעילה. He was arguing from רבי יהודה's position and said: even by your view, at least admit that a storekeeper is like a homeowner. רבי יהודה said no.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר was speaking according to רבי יהודה's view: 'In my view, even if he spent it, he did not commit מעילה. But in your view, at least admit to me that a storekeeper is like a homeowner!' And רבי יהודה answered him: 'No, he is like a money changer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. The idea that 'everyone agrees about spending' was really only רבי יהודה's view. רבי מאיר himself holds there is no מעילה even if the money is spent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר was making a 'by your own rules' argument. He did not accept that spending causes מעילה, but he argued that even if you do accept it, a storekeeper should be treated like a homeowner. So the משנה does not prove that רבי מאיר holds a mistaken sale works, and רב חסדא's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He was speaking according to the other person's view

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי מאיר really holds a storekeeper who spends the money committed מעילה. In his own view, nobody commits מעילה by spending it here. The storekeeper argument was only a 'by your rules' point aimed at רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, for רבי מאיר a mistaken use of הקדש money does nothing at all. The woman is not betrothed, a purchase does not take effect, and the money stays holy. The storekeeper משנה does not disprove this, because there רבי מאיר was arguing on רבי יהודה's terms.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר לִדְבָרָיו דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir was speaking according to Rabbi Yehuda's view:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי, אִם הוֹצִיא נָמֵי לֹא מָעַל,
phrases.english: 'In my view, even if he spent it, he did not commit misuse of Temple property,'
'but in your view,'

phrases.aramaic: אוֹדִי לִי מִיהָא דְּחֶנְוָנִי כְּבַעַל הַבַּיִת!
phrases.english: 'at least admit to me that a storekeeper is like a homeowner!'
And he said to him: 'No, he is like a money changer.'
phrases.notes: The speaker here is רבי יהודה, answering רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר לִדְבָרָיו דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 13 by reading רבי מאיר's words as an argument made on רבי יהודה's terms.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that 'everyone agrees' spending the money is מעילה. That premise belongs only to רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumed רבי מאיר accepted the premise about spending. In fact he was only arguing within רבי יהודה's view, and in his own view spending does not cause מעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps רב חסדא's ruling consistent: for רבי מאיר, a mistaken use of הקדש money does not take effect in any kind of transaction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the משנה: רבי מאיר's words were argued on רבי יהודה's terms and do not reflect his own view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both תנאים seem to agree that spending the money is מעילה, a mistaken purchase with הקדש money would take effect even for רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר himself, spending the money is not מעילה, so רב חסדא's ruling that a mistaken sale does not take effect stands.

steps.title: רב begins a new statement about the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a statement from רב. It sets up his explanation of the reasons behind the rulings of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It tells us that רב is about to speak, and his words will explain the reasoning behind the dispute we just saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא now returns to the משנה's dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about betrothing with הקדש on purpose or by mistake (step 3). It brings in an אמורא, רב, to explain why each one holds his view. This line has only the introduction. The content of רב's statement comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A statement or teaching given by an אמורא.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for רב's point in this line. 'אָמַר רַב' only tells you who is speaking. What he actually says comes in the next line.

phrases.english: Rav says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about the storekeeper משנה ends in step 14, the גמרא returns to the משנה's dispute from step 3 and brings in רב to explain the reasoning of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introductory attribution only. רב's ruling about the reasoning of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה follows in the next line.
